selected_reference_revisions.prompt:
Create a single full-body revised Breachline animal reference painting, landscape 3:2, 1536 × 1024, on warm ivory with a little natural ground and one small plain adult human at a safe distance for scale. Use ONLY the specified cell of the attached six-animal sheet as the edit target; isolate that animal into this standalone painting and ignore all other cells. Preserve its recognizable identity, proportions, covering, colours, pose and scale except for the requested change. All feet and tail entirely visible with generous breathing room. Traditional oil/acrylic fantasy art, selective visible brushwork, matte materials, coherent readable daylight; no photoreal texture noise, uniform microdetail or glossy toy finish. No labels, text, framing, equipment, combat, gore or new mouth appendages.
TARGET: TOP LEFT, the enormous reclining russet-and-cream Highneck, with long raised muscular neck, compact head and huge gathered forelimbs. The previous revision is still not predatory enough. Make the face clearly MORE PREDATORY while preserving the liked body and raised-neck resting pose: a stronger biting jaw, focused forward-directed gaze, pronounced carnivorous teeth with a few substantial canines visible in a slightly parted mouth. Teeth should have believable roots and jaw clearance. Give it the contained confidence of a powerful carnivore, not a scream or a grotesque monster. Keep the compact head recognizably related to the source and integrated into its neck; preserve the warm mottled coat, rounded hindbody, large forelimbs and immense settled weight.
selected_reference_revisions.title: Highneck · stronger predator
selected_reference_revisions.description: The raised neck and settled heavyweight body now carry a stronger carnivorous jaw with prominent biting teeth and a more intent gaze. This develops the predatory direction you requested while keeping the liked silhouette and mottled covering.
selected_reference_revisions.assistant_review: Checked stronger jaw and visible teeth, integrated face/neck, retained low resting body and massive forelimbs, coat continuity and complete framing. No dangling mouthparts or obvious anatomy defects.

selected_reference_revisions.prompt: Make a small local edit to this animal painting: give BOTH FRONT PAWS believable BEAR CLAWS. Retain the broad, heavy, furred paw structure, but replace the tiny catlike claw tips with a clearly visible row of stout non-retractile claws like a brown bear's forepaws. Each claw has a thick base, moderate forward length and a gentle downward curve, naturally growing from a short thick toe. They should look powerful for digging and traction, proportional to the paw. Keep the toes compact and joined into a broad padded paw; no long separated bird fingers, no dramatically hooked raptor talons, and no oversized sickle claws. Preserve the front legs above the paws, all leg positions, both rear feet, head, closed muzzle, neck, crest, feather mantle, body, tail, colours, human scale figure, ground, lighting and framing. Only refine the two front paws and claws. Retain the painted fantasy finish, 3:2 landscape format, with no text.
selected_reference_revisions.reference_role: Entire v4 as edit target; front bear claws only.
selected_reference_revisions.title: Feathered heavyweight · bear claws
selected_reference_revisions.description: The broad furred front paws now carry stout, visible bear-like claws with moderate projection and a gentle curve. The compact toes, sturdy legs, feathered body, closed muzzle and rear feet retain their earlier design.
selected_reference_revisions.assistant_review: Visually compared with v4: front claws are clearly larger and stouter than the small tips, yet stay proportionate and gently curved. Broad compact furred paws remain grounded; no raptor fingers or sickle talons. Upper legs, rear feet, body, face, feather silhouette, scale figure, pose and composition retain their design. No obvious generation defect requiring another pass.

history.prompt: Edit this Breachline animal reference with one local correction: BOTH FRONT FEET become broad, substantial mammalian PAWS. Think of the grounded weight of large feline or bear forepaws: a compact padded mass, four rounded toes grouped closely together, a softly furred top blending into the wrist, and only tiny short claw tips. The paws should feel powerful and able to support this heavyweight. They are not bird talons, grasping hands, elongated fingers or splayed reptile toes. Keep the paws planted naturally; do not show their undersides to the viewer. Preserve the muscular front legs above the wrists and the two rear feet exactly in design. Preserve the entire remaining animal—closed muzzle, head, crest, high neck, feathered body, colouring, leg positions and tail—as well as pose, human scale figure, ground, lighting, composition and painted treatment. No other redesign. Same landscape 3:2 format. No text or labels.
history.reference_role: Entire v2 as edit target, before the excessive talon pass; only front feet change.
history.title: Feathered heavyweight · front paws
history.description: Both front feet are now broad, compact paws with rounded toes, furred tops and only short claw tips. The sturdy legs, feathered body, closed muzzle, pose and rear feet retain their established design.
history.assistant_review: Compared with v2 edit source and v3 feedback: both front feet now read clearly as padded mammalian paws, with rounded grouped toes and short claw tips. Forelegs blend into furred wrists; feet are grounded and coherent. Head, crest, feather mantle, torso, rear feet, four-limb arrangement, scale figure, lighting and composition retained. No long grasping digits or hooked talons remain at the front.

history.prompt: Edit the attached Breachline feathered heavyweight reference. Change ONLY BOTH FRONT FEET / CLAWED FOREHANDS at lower left and lower centre: give them a clearly more claw-like, raptorial structure, with distinct powerful articulated digits and substantially longer, sharply curved keratin talons. The claws should read as functional grasping/raking weapons, organically rooted in the toes, with robust bases and tapering hooked tips. Keep their scale proportionate to this enormous animal, maintain believable wrist-to-digit connections and weight-bearing ground contact. Do not just lengthen rounded toenails; make the forefeet's overall shape more clearly a powerful claw. The two rear feet on the right remain unchanged. Preserve the revised muscular forelegs above the wrists, all four leg positions, body, feather mantle, crest, closed muzzle, neck, tail, pose, scale figure, ground, colours, light, framing and painted treatment. No extra digits or limbs, no mouth change, no dangling mouthparts. Same landscape 3:2 format, no text or labels.
history.reference_role: Entire M21-23 v2 as edit target; only front feet change.
history.title: Feathered heavyweight · front claws
history.description: Both front feet now form pronounced grasping claws, with distinct jointed digits and long hooked talons. The revised muscular legs, feathered body and closed muzzle remain, while the rear feet retain their earlier shape.
history.assistant_review: Visually compared with v2: both front feet now have elongated articulated digits and markedly longer curved talons. The wrists connect coherently, claw bases and tips are readable, and the feet remain grounded. Rear feet, four-legged support, muscular upper forelegs, face, feather mantle, crest, scale figure, pose and composition remain recognizable and unchanged in design. No gross mouthparts or extra limbs.
